title: Floating and Sinking
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A basin of water and a tray of objects: a stone, a nail, a wooden spoon, a plastic bottle (empty and full), a ball of plasticine and the same plasticine shaped into a boat. The child predicts, tests and records in a table before any rule is given.

skills.key_step: The child tests and records whether an object floats (stays at the surface) or sinks (goes to the bottom), and predicts from what it is made of and its shape, not from its weight alone.

floor.prerequisite: Knows that water is a liquid.
floor.question: Does water take the shape of its container?

representations: a basin and a tray of objects
steps: Put the object gently in the water.
Watch: does it stay at the surface or go to the bottom?
Record and compare with the prediction.

board.do: Draw a table: object, prediction, result.
Write a nail, a big log and a small stone.
Write the results: the big log floats, the nail and stone sink.

misconceptions.ask: Which is heavier: a big log or a nail? Which floats?
misconceptions.repair: Weight alone does not decide; a heavy log floats.

misconceptions.ask: Does a metal sufuria lid float if placed flat and gently?
misconceptions.repair: Shape matters too; some metal objects float.

listen_for: it will float in the lake
misconceptions.ask: Does a stone sink in a basin and in a lake?
misconceptions.repair: The amount of water does not change floating or sinking.

listen_for: most of it is under water so it sinks
misconceptions.repair: Staying at the surface is floating.

checks.question: A nail is put in water. Does it float or sink?
A big log floats but a small stone sinks. Does weight alone decide?

skills.key_step: The child names what affects floating: the material, the shape (a hollow or flat shape floats better), the load carried, and tests one factor at a time.

floor.prerequisite: Can tell whether an object floats or sinks.
floor.question: Does a stone float or sink?

representations: a ball of plasticine and the same plasticine as a boat
an empty and a full bottle
steps: Change only one thing at a time.
Same plasticine, different shape: ball sinks, boat floats.
Same bottle, empty or full: empty floats higher.
Add a load to a floating boat until it sinks.
contexts: a bottle used as a float
a sufuria floating in a basin

board.do: Draw the same plasticine shaped as a boat.
Ask whether the boat will float.
Draw the boat floating and write "shape".

misconceptions.ask: What happened to the plasticine boat?
misconceptions.repair: Shape matters: a hollow shape can float.

misconceptions.ask: A ship is heavy. Does it float?
misconceptions.repair: Material and shape matter, not weight alone.

misconceptions.ask: Does a small piece of wood float like a big one?
misconceptions.repair: Pieces of the same material act the same.

misconceptions.ask: What happened as we added coins to the boat?
misconceptions.repair: Too much load makes a floater sink.

checks.question: Why does plasticine float as a boat but sink as a ball?
checks.answer: its shape changed; the hollow boat shape floats

checks.question: A floating boat is loaded with stones until it sinks. What factor changed?

skills.key_step: The child explains uses of floating and sinking (boats and ships, life jackets and rings, floats on nets, anchors and net weights) by the shape or material that makes them float or sink.

floor.prerequisite: Knows shape and material affect floating.
floor.question: Does a hollow boat shape float?

representations: a fishing net with floats and weights
a life jacket or a plastic bottle float
a chart: use, floats or sinks, why
steps: Life jackets: light material or air floats and holds you up.
Net floats and weights: top up, bottom down.
Anchors: heavy, solid metal sinks to hold a boat still.

board.do: Draw a fishing net in water with floats and weights.

board.say: Why are these at the top?

board.do: Wait for "to hold the net up".
Write "floats hold it up, weights pull it down".

misconceptions.repair: A steel ship floats because of its hollow shape full of air.

misconceptions.ask: Does a boat weigh nothing on the shore?
misconceptions.repair: Floating things have weight; water holds them up.

misconceptions.ask: What did the empty bottle do when you pushed it down?
misconceptions.repair: Life jackets are full of light material or air.

misconceptions.ask: Where would the net be with no floats?
misconceptions.repair: Floats keep the top of the net up.

checks.question: Why does a steel ship float when a steel nail sinks?
Give one use of an object that sinks.
checks.answer: an anchor, or weights on a fishing net
